text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Friday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The ratification in Italy of Lithuania's association agreement with the EU got caught up in internal Italian politics when some political forces attempted to use the agreement as a pretext to initiate federal reform. The agreement was ratified on Tuesday

- The leader of the Centre Union Romualdas Ozolas said on Thursday that if the relations with the ruling coalition of the Homeland Union and Christian Democrats became increasingly tense then its ministers might be recalled from the cabinet.
- The head of the privatisation agency said on Thursday that foreign investors are interested in companies where they can privatise more than 51 percent of stake.
- The government is expected to give priorities to strategic investors in the near future.
- Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas expressed his dissatisfaction with the new procedures for the appointment of a prosecutor general passed by parliament earlier this week.
- An opinion poll by Baltic Surveys showed the growing popularity of President Algirdas Brazauskas in February. He headed a list of 10 politicians with 56 percent of approval rating.
- New Finance Minister Algirdas Shemeta said in an interview to the newspaper that one of his aims is to avoid abrupt changes in the finance system of the country.
- The government wants to keep a 34 percent stake in Butinge oil terminal.
- The privatisation agency said only 30 out of 835 companies on the 1997 privatisation list may be attractive to foreign investors.

- In government circles it is expected that Lithuanian Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius and the chairman of the Bank of Lithuania Reinoldijus Sharkinas will sign a letter to the head of the IMF before March 1 to say Lithuania will increase some excise duties, will not rush changes to the monetary system and will make troubled bank Innovation Bank bankrupt.
- The closing of Innovation bank will cost the state nearly one billion litas, the newspaper says.
